hints: A valid combination uses dictionary words that concatenate exactly to the target string.
Let dp[i] count ways to form the first i characters.
For each endpoint, check dictionary words that end there and add dp before each matching word.
analogy: For each possible last word, count the ways to build everything before it.
example: If target 'ab' has words 'a','b','ab', it can be formed as ['a','b'] or ['ab'], giving 2 ways.
algorithm: Store dictionary words in a trie. Set dp[0]=1; from each reachable position i, walk trie along the target and add dp[i] to dp[j+1] whenever a word ends there, modulo 1e9+7.
correctness: Every decomposition has one final word; removing it leaves a unique valid decomposition of a shorter prefix, so summing all matching final words counts every decomposition once.
complexity: O(L*W) worst case for target length L and max word length W; O(total dictionary characters+L) space.
